name: Email and Phishing Hunt
author: Threat Intelligence Team
prerequisites: Exchange Admin or Global Reader role for message trace access
Microsoft 365 Defender or Proofpoint / Mimecast admin access
Email gateway (MTA) log access for the hunt window
required_tools: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Threat Explorer
Splunk with O365 Management Activity log index
PhishTank / URLScan.io / VirusTotal for URL analysis

hunt_actions.title: Phishing Campaign Detection
actions: Search for phishing emails using Microsoft 365 Threat Explorer: Navigate to https://security.microsoft.com > Email & Collaboration > Explorer > filter by Detection Technology = Anti-phishing, Anti-malware, or URL detonation > set time range to hunt window > group by SenderDomain > export to CSV. Review sender domains for typosquatting or newly registered domains.

Hunt for emails with malicious URLs that bypassed ATP: `Connect-ExchangeOnline; Search-UnifiedAuditLog -RecordType ThreatIntelligence -Operations AtpDetection -StartDate '2025-01-01' -EndDate '2025-04-01' | ConvertFrom-Json | Select CreationDate, UserIds, AuditData | Export-Csv atp_detections.csv` — also submit clicked URLs to URLScan.io: `curl -s -X POST https://urlscan.io/api/v1/scan/ -H 'API-Key: <key>' -d '{"url":"<url>","visibility":"private"}'`

Identify email addresses targeted in the same phishing campaign: `Search-UnifiedAuditLog -RecordType ThreatIntelligence -StartDate '2025-03-01' -EndDate '2025-04-01' | ForEach { $a=ConvertFrom-Json $_.AuditData; $a } | Group-Object SenderAddress | Sort Count -Desc | Select -First 20 | Select Name, Count` — a single sender targeting multiple internal recipients indicates a campaign.

Check for homograph and lookalike domain abuse in email headers: `Get-MessageTrace -StartDate '2025-03-01' -EndDate '2025-04-01' -PageSize 5000 | Where-Object { $_.SenderAddress -notmatch '@approvedomain\.com' } | Select-Object Received, SenderAddress, RecipientAddress, Subject | Export-Csv external_senders.csv` — then visually inspect sender domains for Unicode lookalikes or character substitution.

hunt_actions.title: Business Email Compromise (BEC) Indicators
actions: Hunt for inbox rules forwarding email externally: `Get-InboxRule -Mailbox <user> | Where-Object { $_.ForwardTo -or $_.ForwardAsAttachmentTo -or $_.RedirectTo } | Select Name, ForwardTo, ForwardAsAttachmentTo, RedirectTo` — or for all mailboxes: `Get-Mailbox -ResultSize Unlimited | ForEach { Get-InboxRule -Mailbox $_.UserPrincipalName | Where-Object { $_.ForwardTo -or $_.RedirectTo } | Select Mailbox:$_.UserPrincipalName, Name, ForwardTo, RedirectTo }`. Any external forwarding rule is a critical finding.

Detect mailbox delegation or full access permissions added: `Get-MailboxPermission -Identity <mailbox> | Where-Object { $_.AccessRights -contains 'FullAccess' -and $_.IsInherited -eq $false -and $_.User -notlike 'NT AUTHORITY*' }` — and: `Get-RecipientPermission -Identity <mailbox> | Where-Object { $_.Trustee -ne 'NT AUTHORITY\SELF' }` for SendAs permissions. Audit log: `Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations 'Add-MailboxPermission' -StartDate '2025-01-01'`

Hunt for email exfiltration to personal accounts: Splunk: `index=o365 Operation=Send | where tostring(recipients{}) match '(@gmail\.com|@yahoo\.com|@protonmail\.com|@outlook\.com)' AND isnotnull(itemSubject) | stats count by userPrincipalName, recipients | sort -count` — executive mailboxes sending to personal email domains require immediate investigation.

Identify spoofed internal sender domains not failing SPF/DKIM/DMARC: `Get-MessageTrace -StartDate '2025-03-01' -EndDate '2025-04-01' | Where-Object { $_.SenderAddress -match '@yourdomain\.com' -and $_.FromIP -notmatch '<your_mail_server_IP_range>' } | Select SenderAddress, RecipientAddress, FromIP, Subject` — internal domain spoofing from external IPs that passes anti-spoofing indicates misconfigured SPF records.

hunt_actions.title: Malicious Attachment Analysis
actions: Pull quarantined messages with malicious attachments from Defender: `Get-QuarantineMessage -QuarantineTypes Malware -StartReceivedDate '2025-03-01' -EndReceivedDate '2025-04-01' | Select SenderAddress, RecipientAddress, Subject, Received, QuarantineTypes | Export-Csv quarantine_malware.csv` — extract attachment hashes and submit to VirusTotal: `curl -s 'https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/<sha256>' -H 'x-apikey: <key>' | jq '.data.attributes.last_analysis_stats'`

Hunt for macro-enabled Office documents delivered via email: In Defender Threat Explorer filter by Attachment File Type = .xlsm, .docm, .xltm, .pptm, .xlam within the hunt window. Also: `Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations 'FileDownloaded,FileAccessed' | Where-Object { $_.AuditData -match '\.(xlsm|docm|pptm|xlam)' }` — document when these were opened and by whom.

Identify HTML smuggling attacks (large HTML attachments): `Get-MessageTraceDetail -MessageTraceId <id> | Where-Object { $_.Detail -match 'HTML attachment' }` — or filter email gateway logs for attachments with .html or .htm extension > 50KB. Submit suspicious HTML files to `urlscan.io` or analyze with `grep -oP 'atob\(.*?\)' suspicious.html` to find base64-encoded payloads inside.

questions: Are Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 (or equivalent) Safe Links and Safe Attachments policies enabled for all users, including shared mailboxes and distribution groups?
Are SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records published and enforced (DMARC policy set to p=quarantine or p=reject) for all sending domains, including subdomain and third-party sending service domains?
Is the Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log enabled for all users, and are audit logs retained for a minimum of 180 days (requires E3/E5 or the Purview Audit Standard license)?

Is there a documented and tested phishing reporting mechanism for end users (e.g., Microsoft Report Message add-in, KnowBe4 PAB), and are reported messages triaged by the security team within a defined SLA?
Are inbox rules monitored for external forwarding configurations on a scheduled basis, and is an alert configured in Defender or Sentinel to fire when a new external forwarding rule is created?

Has executive leadership (CEO, CFO, General Counsel) been enrolled in targeted anti-phishing policy with stricter thresholds in Defender for Office 365 to account for Business Email Compromise targeting?
Are all email-sending third-party services (marketing platforms, HR systems, ticketing tools) authorized via SPF include statements and DKIM key delegation, with the full inventory documented?
Is user security awareness training conducted at a minimum annually with phishing simulation exercises, and are click rates tracked and used to target remedial training for high-risk users?
